predecessors.name: Western Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania, granted by Honorius to the Visigothic federates under Wallia in 418

successors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
successors.text: the peninsula and Septimania conquered by the Umayyads 711-721 (Visigothic Kingdom page: 'Most of the Visigothic Kingdom was conquered by Umayyad troops from North Africa in 711 to 719'; Septimania…

successors.name: Kingdom of Asturias
successors.text: the unconquered north: Pelagius 'revolted in 718, and defeated the Muslims at the battle of Covadonga' (Visigothic Kingdom page; the Umayyad page dates Covadonga 722)

ledger.x: 418: Honorius settles the Visigoths under Wallia in the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania.
451: the settlements spread over Aquitania II, Novempopulana and Narbonensis.
456: the Goths take the Spanish provinces after the Orbigo.
459: the Goths leave Spain.
461: Narbonne.
469: Merida and the west of the peninsula.
471: Berry and a foothold in Provence.
472: Tarraconensis.
475: Clermont and Auvergne.
475: Nepos gives up the Barcelona region.
475: Provence.
507: Vouillé.
507: the court leaves Toulouse for Barcelona, 'temporarily'.
508: the rest of Gaul but Septimania.
510: Provence leaves the Visigothic shape.
511: Gesalec is deposed and Theodoric the Great takes the Visigothic Kingdom under his direct control as regent for his grandson Amalaric.
542: the capital moves from Barcelona to Toledo (infobox: 'Toledo (542-711)').
551: Athanagild takes Seville.
554: Agila dies and Athanagild is sole ruler, so the rebel land rejoins the kingdom.
555: the Byzantine province of Spania.
569: Liuvigild's first campaign against the Suebi.
571: Medina Sidonia.
572: Cordoba.
574: Amaya and the City of Cantabria destroyed.
577: Orospeda.
580: Baetica rises under Hermenegild.
582: Merida. Liuvigild 'captured Merida', which had been under Bishop Masona's control since the early 570s.
584: Seville falls and the revolt ends.
585: the Suebi kingdom is conquered.
602: the northern strip fills in.
612: the northern strip fills in further.
615: Malaga. 'In 614 and 615, he carried out two massive expeditions against them and conquered Malaga before 619' (Sisebut).
624: the Byzantines are expelled from the peninsula.
661: the Pyrenean belt of the Ebro and Rioja leaves the shape.
711: the Umayyads land and win the Guadalete.
712: Merida falls.
712: Seville, Cordoba and Toledo.
713: Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza.
714: the rest of the peninsula.
714: the fighting for the south and centre ends; the Umayyads hold the peninsula but for the mountains of the north and Ardo's Septimania ('As of 713 (or 714), the last Visigothic king, Ardo').
717: the first Umayyad forays into Septimania, under al-Hurr ibn Abd al-Rahman.
720: Narbonne falls.
721: Ardo dies and Septimania passes to the Umayyads.
721: the Visigothic Kingdom ends with Ardo and the fall of Septimania; 'Most of the Visigothic Kingdom was conquered by Umayyad troops from North Africa in 711 to 719'.

wars.name: Gothic attacks on Narbonne and Toulouse
wars.outcome: Theodoric I's attack on Narbonne in 436 was stopped by Litorius, who drove the Goths back to Toulouse; 'in 439 at the Battle of Toulouse the Visigoths defeated the allied forces of Romans and Huns'.

wars.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
wars.outcome: Visigoths and Romans defeat Attila's Huns; Theodoric I is killed.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign against the Suebi
wars.outcome: Theodoric II defeats the Suebi at the Orbigo, takes Braga and plunders Gallaecia; the Goths then hold the Spanish provinces (ledger 456).

wars.name: Majorian's war against the Visigoths
wars.outcome: Majorian defeated the Goths at Arles; in the peace the Goths gave up their Spanish settlements and returned to Aquitaine.

wars.name: Euric's Gallic and Hispanic campaigns
wars.outcome: Euric wins the battle near Arles (471), Berry, most of Hispania (472), Clermont (475); in 475 Nepos recognises his independence and renounces Provence and the Barcelona region.

wars.name: Battle of Vouillé
wars.outcome: Clovis defeats and kills Alaric II 'around spring 507'; the Franks take Aquitaine and Toulouse, the Visigoths keep Septimania.

wars.name: Visigothic civil war of Agila and Athanagild
wars.outcome: Athanagild rebels in 551, takes Seville and asks Justinian for help; the Byzantines land (552) and Agila is defeated, then dies in 554.

wars.name: Byzantine-Visigothic wars in Spania
wars.outcome: Spania held 552-624; Leovigild retakes Medina Sidonia and Cordoba (571-572) and Orospeda (577), Sisebut Malaga (614-615), Suintila the last towns (624).

wars.name: Liuvigild's reconquest and the Suebi
wars.outcome: Liuvigild subdues Zamora, Palencia and Leon (569), the south (570-577), the Cantabri (574), Mérida (582) and ends the Suebic kingdom in 585.

wars.name: Revolt of Hermenegild
wars.outcome: Liuvigild takes Merida (582) and Seville (584); Hermenegild is imprisoned and executed on 13 April 585; the Byzantines withdrew after Liuvigild paid 30,000 pieces of gold.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
wars.outcome: Guadalete (July 711); Merida 712; Seville, Cordoba, Toledo 712; Leon, Astorga, Zaragoza 713; Ardo holds Septimania until his death in 721; Narbonne falls 719 or 720.

certainty.note: The grants of 418, 461 and 475 are by province or city, not by surveyed line; the Suebi, Basque, Cantabrian and Byzantine-coast frontiers are approximate, and the Pyrenean frontier with the Franks after 507 is a band, not a line.
